sections.h2: Where is Laclede County, Missouri, and what towns does it include?
sections.html:
Laclede County sits in the Ozarks of south central Missouri, with Lebanon as the county seat and largest city. Wikipedia lists 768 square miles of total area, of which 765 is land, and part of the Mark Twain National Forest lies inside the county line.

The county was organized on February 24, 1849 and carries the name of Pierre Laclede, the founder of St. Louis. Camden, Pulaski, Texas, Wright, Webster and Dallas counties surround it. The Census Bureau counted 36,039 people in 2020 and estimated 36,943 for July 2025.

Beyond Lebanon, the incorporated places are Conway, Richland, Phillipsburg, Stoutland and Evergreen, and Bennett Springs is a census-designated place. Anyone selling a house here will deal with one of those city halls or with the unincorporated county, so check which applies to your parcel before you list.

sections.h2: What is the county government like in Laclede County?
sections.html:
Laclede County is a statutory third class county, and its offices work out of the Laclede County Government Center in Lebanon. The county's own site traces the courthouse story: the first permanent building went up in 1851, a second one in 1894 burned in 1920, and a replacement finished in 1925 for $72,428.

A law enforcement sales tax passed in August 1994 paid for the current building. The same page reports a 2024 assessed valuation of $549,845,759, compared with $20,234,001 in 1960. The collector and the assessor both run online record lookups.

Five public school districts touch the county: Lebanon R-III, Laclede County R-I at Conway, Gasconade C-4 at Falcon, Joel E. Barber C-5, and Stoutland R-II. The district that serves your address sets part of the levy on your bill, so the district name matters when you compare two houses.

sections.h2: What do the numbers say about housing in Laclede County?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau's QuickFacts page puts the median owner-occupied home in Laclede County at $168,400 for 2020 to 2024, with 68.2% of homes lived in by their owners.

  • Households: 14,558, averaging 2.48 people
  • Housing units: 16,211 as of July 2025
  • Median household income: $53,282 (2024 dollars)
  • Median gross rent: $809
  • Median monthly owner cost with a mortgage: $1,160, and $405 without one
  • Mean commute: 21.4 minutes

A homeowner with no mortgage has no escrow account paying the bill, so the statement from the collector is the only prompt to pay it.

sections.h2: Who sets and who collects property tax in Laclede County?
sections.html:
Two offices split the work: the Assessor sets the value, and the Collector of Revenue bills and collects the tax. The collector's site says the office must collect strictly from the assessor's records and cannot change a bill, so a wrong acreage, owner name or parcel description goes to the Assessor at (417) 532-7163.

The Collector's office collects current and delinquent real estate and personal property tax plus merchant license fees and railroad and utility tax. The money goes out to schools, road districts, fire protection entities and other local subdivisions. The office also processes escrow payments from mortgage companies.

Laclede County's collector site offers searches by owner name, parcel number, street address or account number, plus payment history for each account. Pull your parcel record before you list the house so you know what is owed and which year it covers.

sections.h2: When are Laclede County tax bills mailed and due?
sections.html:
Bills are mailed every November and are due by December 31. The Collector's office starts printing statements in late October, after the County Clerk hands over the current year's tax books, and it mails separate statements for personal property and real estate.

Office hours are 8am to 4pm, Monday through Friday, and the office closes for state and federal holidays. A paid receipt comes back by mail after processing. If you pay after December 31, the delinquency schedule printed on your statement shows what you owe. Ask the office at the number on your bill for the penalty amount, since the page does not list percentages.

Payment can be made in several ways:

  • In the office with cash, personal check, money order or cashier's check
  • By mail with the return envelope (never send cash)
  • Online or by phone with a credit card, which adds a convenience fee
  • In the payment drop box at the Second Street entrance of the courthouse, available at any hour

One check can cover both the personal and real estate statements.

sections.h2: How do I pay in installments or get senior relief in Laclede County?
sections.html:
The Collector runs a prepay installment program: ten equal payments based on last year's tax, then an eleventh payment for the remaining balance. Only automated bank drafts are accepted, delinquent accounts cannot enroll, and a parcel whose tax runs through a mortgage escrow cannot join. Call (417) 532-4301 to ask about enrolling.

Senior homeowners may qualify for a credit that locks the homestead real estate tax at its first-year level. The collector's page spells out the rules: one home only, lived in as a primary residence, renewal every year between April 1 and the last Friday in May, and no retroactive savings. The credit in the first application year is always zero, and the first real reduction appears the following year. The county's home page notes that 2026 applications have closed, so a new applicant waits for the next window.

The credit is not an exemption, so the owner still pays tax on the home. If you are weighing a sale, ask the collector how a sale affects your enrollment.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Laclede County assessment?
sections.html:
Start with the Assessor, then go to the county Board of Equalization, then to the State Tax Commission. The Board of Equalization appeal is due by the second Monday in July, and the State Tax Commission appeal is due 30 days after the date on the Board's decision letter.

You can also pay first and dispute later. The State Tax Commission's guidance says to pay the whole bill to the collector by December 31, write "paid under protest" on the check, and file a written statement that gives your grounds and your opinion of fair market value. A mailed payment and statement count if they carry a postmark no later than December 31.

If the property sits in the name of an LLC, trust, corporation or estate, an attorney must file the State Tax Commission appeal. Anyone settling a parent's estate before a sale should note that restriction early.

sections.h2: What happens if Laclede County taxes go unpaid?
sections.html:
The land goes onto the list for the annual delinquent tax certificate sale, held on the fourth Monday in August at 10 a.m. at the Laclede County Courthouse, 200 N. Adams in Lebanon. The list runs in a local newspaper for three consecutive weeks beforehand, and an owner can pay the taxes, penalty, interest and costs at any time before the parcel sells.

A winning bidder receives a certificate of purchase, not a deed. The owner has one year from the sale date to redeem by paying the base amount on the certificate plus 10% annual interest, along with any later taxes the buyer paid. The collector asks for 24 hours' notice before a redemption and suggests allowing 20 minutes at the counter.

If no one redeems, the certificate holder may apply for a collector's deed after notifying lienholders and the owner by certified mail at least 90 days earlier. Liens are not wiped out at the sale itself. Surplus bid money above the taxes and costs belongs to the owner of record.

sections.h2: What should I check before selling a house with tax due in Laclede County?
sections.html:
Look up the parcel on the collector's portal, confirm which years are paid, and order a title search so nothing surprises you at closing. Ask your title company to pay any past-due bill from the sale proceeds and to prorate the current year under your contract.

  • If you bought the property before October, the statement may have gone to the prior owner, so check with them or the collector's office.
  • If the house sits on a delinquent list and the August sale is close, pay before the sale date.
  • If you have a tax installment plan or senior credit, tell the collector about the sale.
  • If the value on your notice looks wrong, contact the Assessor before the July appeal deadline.

Get the payoff figure from the collector in writing before closing.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Laclede County, Missouri?
faqs.a: They are due by December 31. Bills go out in November, and a payment after that date follows the delinquency schedule printed on the statement.

faqs.q: Who do I call about a wrong value on my Laclede County tax bill?
faqs.a: Call the County Assessor at (417) 532-7163. The collector's office cannot change a bill because it must collect from the assessor's records.

faqs.q: Can I pay my Laclede County property tax online?
faqs.a: Yes. The Collector of Revenue site accepts online card payments, and a convenience fee applies. You can also pay by phone, by mail, in person, or in the courthouse drop box.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to appeal a Laclede County assessment?
faqs.a: The Board of Equalization appeal is due by the second Monday in July. If the Board rules against you, the State Tax Commission appeal is due 30 days from the date on the Board's letter.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Laclede County house if the taxes are behind?
faqs.a: Yes. Get a payoff figure from the collector and have the title company pay it from the proceeds at closing. If the August tax sale is near, paying the balance first keeps the parcel off the sale.
